svg.title: TOPAK D4 — Privileged paths through the floor, and the forensic floor that survives them
svg.desc: Two paths cannot be written as subtractions: break-glass adds authority, erasure destroys authority-bearing evidence. ADR-0013 writes them once, as declared floor entries under one authorization model, bounds their number, and checks that they do not compose into an unattributable effect. ADR-0028 names six classes of authority fact that no erasure may reach.
svg.text: TOPAK · D4

text.tspan: Privileged paths through the floor, and the forensic floor that survives them

svg.text: Two paths cannot be written as subtractions: break-glass adds authority, erasure destroys authority-bearing evidence. ADR-0013 writes them once, as declared floor entries under one authorization model, bounds their number, and checks that they do not compose into an unattributable effect. ADR-0028 names six classes of authority fact that no erasure may reach.

Author-ratified. ADR-0013 and ADR-0028 were ratified in genesis on 2026.09.23 by the custodian alone; the move to genesis gave up the independent reviewer the post-bootstrap phase would have supplied, and the first post-bootstrap quorum repays it (ToO §3.3; ADR-0013 open obligations). Anything citing these guarantees says "author-ratified".
An explicit override path, logged, quorum-witnessed and modeled, on the control/data plane split rather than forbidden. Because it adds authority it cannot
be a refining bundle: it is a verified-object exception, changing at deploy cadence.
Must never justify data-plane autonomy in irreversible domains (ADR-0009).
Grants authority within the rules in force and cannot alter them, so it is an effect, not a third kind of authority change (ADR-0015 R2).
Actuate only, by a Run seat, of a tool in the issued breakGlass.tools; never Consult, Report, Vote, Submit or Erase
The break-glass roster in the issued rules, with its quorum k (dev rules: two keys, k = 2)
NC-1 and NC-2, below
R7: no break-glass grant may authorize Issue, Vote or promotion
May narrow it, never widen it (ADR-0030 §5): a bad bundle can disable break-glass, a liveness cost
Floor policy R3-observer-live applies to break-glass too: a dead, partitioned or starved cell Observer stops its Thinker's
break-glass (ADR-0039 §2). Break-glass under a dead Observer is open (G7 item 49)
Each invocation is F5; the reference flags an admit through X1-break-glass without R1-actuate-allowlisted (
via_break_glass)
No TTL. R8 is drafted and pending (ADR-0026 A1, four conditions unmet). At the reference, approvals are scoped to (seat,
epoch) and lapse at the next epoch increment or a targeted revocation of the seat (I9; G10)
An event: consensus-ordered, modeled in TLA+, recorded in the log it modifies. Deletion cannot be an out-of-band operator action, because that is the
capability to rewrite history.
Its authorization predicate lives in the verified object, not in a bundle: erasure operates outside the refinement lattice (09.12 acceptance).
Mechanism: deletion of sealed round topics and of plaintext-store entries; crypto-shredding rejected.
Erase of an ArchiveRecord, under an erasure quorum (context.erasureQuorum)
The erasure roster in the issued rules
NC-1 and NC-2, below
F-forensic-classes forbids Erase of any record of class F1–F6: bundles may only narrow erasure further; removing a
class is a floor relaxation (ADR-0028 §2)
A safety property that separates lawful erasure from history rewriting (ToO §4.3)
Every erasure event is itself F6, which is why demand type 5 is declined
No erasure roster is issued (ADR-0029 §5, ceremony step 5), so erasureQuorum is FALSE from epoch 0 and X2 admits
nothing. The first roster comes after bootstrap under the two-key rule (ADR-0026 §4)
Not built (G11): nothing to exercise, matching the corpus position
Every privileged grant (promotion, break-glass, erasure) is a quorum decision on an anchor-issued roster,
bounded by the rules floor. Erasure and break-glass differ only in roster and envelope.
Privileged is load-bearing: ordinary Run admits are grants too, decided against a bundle, not a roster (S6-13).
Issue: an environment event validated by Authentic and the rules floor; forensic class F4.

text.tspan: Exception count, bounded by rules-floor R6

svg.text: Current count 2; bound 2 (R6 effective 2026.09.23 with ADR-0013; the reference refuses rules with more, rules.rs). Adding a
third is a floor relaxation: an anchor issuance and a promotion. Every carve-out works against floor minimality, which is why the
count is bounded. Open: confirm R6 = 2 is not already at its bound for known future exceptions.
Each exception is a named, versioned entry carrying its action envelope, its roster reference and its
non-composition obligations.
Since ADR-0030 they are Cedar policies inside the floor, as are the six forensic classes, so composition applies
uniformly: a bundle can narrow either exception and widen neither.

text.tspan: Non-composition: NC-1 and NC-2, checked 2026.09.23 and proved 2026.10.02 (ADR-0013 §4, §6, B25)

svg.text: Break-glass chained with erasure never yields an effect that is authorized, erased, and unattributable.
Erasure never removes a record in a forensic-floor class, under any composition with break-glass.

text.tspan: NC2 == \A r \in created : r.kind \in ForensicKinds => r \in retained

svg.text: Mutations change the mechanism, never the property. M1 drops F1 from the erasure envelope's denials, so the authority trail becomes erasable. M2 lets a break-glass grant widen the erasure envelope instead of only narrowing it.

NonComposition.tla (119f9a7e878f8929), TLC2 2.19. The third witness matters: without it NC-1 could hold because the two paths never meet. Scope: two effects, one break-glass invocation, small constants; ForensicKinds = {F1, F5, F6}, three of six

classes. Non-composition and reachability, checked. Since 2026.10.02 NC1 and NC2 are proved for every behaviour of the module, not under M1 or M2 (NonComposition_proof.tla, 58 obligations; ADR-0013 B25). The proof needed a clause the module
never states, that only admitted effects are recorded as via break-glass: no TLC run could see that gap (G8 §3, result 3). Run by the author: evidence, not attestation.

• All six are control-plane facts (ADR-0004) and boundary events (ADR-0020). No cognitive payload is in the floor: prompts, reasoning and review commentary remain erasable.
• No new primitive: each class is a policy-floor denial on the erasure envelope, so bundles can only narrow erasure further; removing a class or shortening the horizon is a floor relaxation (§2).
• Stop attribution is a feedback path, not just evidence: in STPA terms the Observer is a controller, not a probe (ToO §4.4).
• Same monotone shape as the policy floor, in the other direction: the policy floor caps authority, the forensic floor guarantees retention; exceptions may preserve more, never less (Context, E1).

"Immutable" lets a deployment claim conformance after erasing evidence. The archetype property: every admitted boundary event remains readable by the declared audit authority for the declared horizon.
Archetype horizon: the lifetime of the rules-epoch chain. Audit authority: the anchor plus a declared external auditor role (still to define). Shortening either is a legibility degeneracy.
The maximum projection each regime derives from.
Subtracts the record: erasure of payloads, never of F1–F6.
Six-year retention and disclosure accounting are additive and not expressed.
Subtracts the reader set: compartmentation is not erasure while the audit
authority stays a reader.
Conformant except at spill remediation.
"Hide that a record ever existed": declined. It conflicts with NC-2, since the
erasure event is F6.
A deployment needing it is outside the archetype's declared demands.
The roster is withheld by the ceremony itself (ADR-0029 §5, step 5), not by either record's status. Erasure is disabled from epoch 0: fail-closed, and it
costs nothing, since there is nothing to erase yet.
ADR-0006 therefore stands ratified with no path to exercise it until a roster is issued after bootstrap under the two-key rule, by which point ADR-0013 and
ADR-0028 have been through confirmation.

text.tspan: The forensic horizon has a seam at re-genesis

svg.text: The horizon is the lifetime of the rules-epoch chain, and re-genesis starts a new chain, which follows anchor loss or capture: the authority record lapses
exactly when it matters most.
That a successor inherits read access to its predecessor's forensic classes is a re-genesis migration obligation, open (G7 item 10), to be settled before
ADR-0028's confirmation. ADR-0003 A1 lets a successor tell its topics apart, and settles nothing else.
No clause ends an approved break-glass grant: the gap R8 would close (ADR-0026 A1 note; ToO rev 6 §10).
R8 is vacuous until the mechanism reads the TTL; its companion clause would touch a privileged path and carry C1; T_BG has no archetype value;
ADR-0032 §2 puts a break-glass TTL in the trusted-time row.
Reference: approvals lapse at the next epoch increment, so break-glass is time-unbounded within an epoch (G10).
anchor loss or capture → re-genesis; inherited read access: open
